outcome: An object merged with a permanent becomes part of one merged permanent represented by all its components.
A merged permanent has only the characteristics of its topmost component, as a copiable effect.
A merging object leaves its zone without the merged permanent counting as having entered the battlefield, so enters triggers do not fire.
A merged permanent keeps its continuous effects and is not newly under a player's control, as it is the same object.
The merged permanent is a token only if its topmost component is a token.
A merged permanent's face-up or face-down status follows its topmost component, and a face-down permanent turned face up by merging does not count as turned face up.
Turning a merged permanent face down or up turns every component the same way.
A face-down merged permanent containing an instant or sorcery stays face down when it would turn face up and turned-face-up triggers do not fire.
Flipping a merged permanent containing a flip card uses that component's alternative characteristics.
Transforming a merged permanent turns each double-faced component to its other face.
An effect turning a face-up merged permanent containing a double-faced component face down does nothing.
When a merged permanent leaves the battlefield, one permanent leaves and every component goes to the appropriate zone.

note: Arranging the components in the graveyard or library is the owner's choice.
The exiling player determines relative timestamp order.

outcome: An effect finding the new object a merged permanent became finds all components and acts on each.
A replacement effect applied to a leaving merged permanent applies to all its components.
A replacement effect for cards entering a zone applies to all components of a non-token merged permanent, and to only the card components of a token one.
